subject: Elevated user journey & emergency support access — next steps
messages:
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa@redwood.com>
To: Priya Shah <ps@blueharbor.ai>, Mark Liu <mark.liu@edgepay.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 18 Apr 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Elevated user journey & emergency support access — next steps

Hi Priya / Mark — thanks again for the demo earlier. Quick recap of the items we discussed and a couple of clarifying questions so we can prepare the SOC/evidence package and the support access workflow: 

What we heard on the call (high-level):
- You need least-privilege RBAC for analytics-only users vs. admin users; multi-tenant isolation is a requirement.
- Support engineers will need temporary elevated access for on-demand debugging; you prefer a formal "break-glass" workflow with approval and audit logging.
- Residency preference: US region for production datasets.
- Retention expectations: short TTL for raw PII (we discussed 30–90 days) and longer retention for immutable audit logs (180–365 days).
- Tokenized/hashed PII allowed in audit logs; raw PII must be controlled.

Questions / asks for you (if you can confirm in reply):
1) Confirm production residency — US-East vs US-West (we need this to validate available zones and latency).
2) Confirm retention windows for (a) raw input payloads containing PII, (b) inference logs (prompt + response), and (c) audit logs. Please include retention minimums and regulatory must-haves.
3) For break-glass, who should be the approver role (security manager, ops manager, or product owner)? Do you require multi-person approval?
4) Any existing evidence or templates (SLA language, internal incident workflow) you can share now will speed our readiness review.

Attached: support privileges matrix (blank) to capture roles/permissions and a data-flow diagram for the call. Please fill the matrix for one or two representative roles and we’ll validate mappings on our side.

Next steps from Redwood:
- We’ll map the role matrix to our RBAC model and return an annotated version. (Owner: Vivek — ETA 2 business days once we have your matrix.)
- Prepare an example break-glass runbook and the audit log retention profile. (Owner: Marissa — ETA 3 business days.)
- Share SOC2/controls evidence links and a short engineering note on how we isolate KV cache and ephemeral logs.

If helpful I can schedule a 30-min follow-up with Vivek to walk through the matrix in real-time.

Thanks — Tessa

--
Tessa Morgan | Account Executive
Redwood Inference

From: Priya Shah <ps@blueharbor.ai>

Date: Mon, 19 Apr 2027 09:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Elevated user journey & emergency support access — next steps

Thanks Tessa — great session. A few quick answers below and an ask for a sample break-glass SLA.

1) Residency: US-East (primary), US-West as DR only.
2) Retention windows (initial ask):
   - Raw PII payloads: 45 days (we will consider 30 only if tokenization can be guaranteed at write-time).
   - Inference logs (prompt/response): 90 days; after that aggregated usage metrics only.
   - Audit logs (auth, role changes, break-glass events): 365 days.

3) Break-glass approver: Security Manager is preferred; one approver is OK but we need a post-approval review within 72 hours by Ops.

4) Attached is our incident approval template — I can upload it if useful. Also: any sample language for support engineer access windows (time-limited SSH/RBAC elevation) would help.

We filled the matrix for two roles (see attached). Let us know if those map to Redwood roles or if you want a short pairing session.

Best,
Priya

- Retention mapping: raw PII 45d, inference logs 90d, audit logs 365d — feasible? Any caveats for aggregated-only after 90d?

Attaching Priya's filled matrix. If it's easier to jump on a quick 20-min sync I can coordinate.

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Apr 2027 09:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Elevated user journey & emergency support access — next steps

Thanks Tessa — reviewed Priya's matrix and the ask. Quick confirmations and next actions: 

- Residency: US-East primary is fine. We’ll pin the customer namespace to a US-East region and ensure KV cache nodes are colocated; no technical restriction besides standard capacity planning.
- Retention: we can implement the requested windows: raw PII 45d, inference logs 90d then roll to aggregated metrics, audit logs 365d. Note: immutable audit logs are stored in compressed WORM buckets — retrieval latency for deep queries may be higher.
- Break-glass: we support single-approver by default and can add a required post-approval review within 72 hours. Evidence produced per elevated session: approver identity, approver timestamp, session start/end, operator identity, reason text, and a snapshot of actions (API calls / collection identifiers) for the session. We will also emit a structured audit event and a signed attestation file.

Next steps (engineering owners / ETAs):
- Annotate the customer matrix with Redwood role mappings and permission IDs (I will drop the annotated file in the Drive link by EOD tomorrow).
- Draft break-glass runbook + sample SLA wording (Marissa to circulate in ~3 business days).
- Provide the SOC2 control mapping extract and a short note on how we handle tokenization vs raw PII at ingestion (I’ll include the engineer note in the Drive folder).

I attached a small checklist of the evidence items we can provide for procurement/security reviews. If Priya wants a short call to walk the annotated matrix I can join.

Vivek
